content: In regions without access to fluoridated public water supplies and with limited public dental care for children, participants in a study were selected from families earning up to two Brazilian minimum wages (approximately $208 per year). Children aged 18 to 42 months were eligible if their parents consented to their participation. The study included two groups: children breastfed for less than 12 months (non-exposed group) and those still being breastfed at the time of examination (exposed group). Exclusion criteria included children with debilitating systemic diseases reported by their parents or those who had received antibiotics in the last 30 days, as this could interfere with the colonization of mutans streptococci. Mothers or guardians completed a validated questionnaire to collect demographic data, and a 24-hour food recall interview was conducted to assess dietary information. A single calibrated professional clinically evaluated carious lesions, and the decayed, missing, and filled teeth (dmft) score was calculated for each child. A 15% random sample of household addresses was selected, and trained fieldworkers enumerated individuals in each household. All children aged 6 to 14 years were invited to participate. Parents completed a supervised questionnaire for each child, collecting data on breastfeeding duration categorized as breastfed for less than 6 months, 6 to 12 months, or more than 12 months. In another study, the Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort (Raine) Study recruited 2,900 pregnant women and followed their live births for 14 years. Inclusion criteria required a gestational age of 16 to 20 weeks, English proficiency, an expectation to deliver at the hospital, and intent to remain in Western Australia for long-term follow-up. A cross-sectional study conducted in Turkey included postmenopausal women aged 45 to 75 years who underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans. Exclusion criteria included a history of drug or alcohol abuse, high caffeine intake, or conditions affecting bone metabolism. Participants were interviewed face-to-face using a detailed questionnaire covering prior pregnancies, breastfeeding history, and medical and demographic information. Breastfeeding duration was analyzed as total lifetime breastfeeding and average duration per child. In Lagos, Nigeria, preschool children attending immunization and well-baby clinics were randomly selected for a study. Mothers completed a pre-tested structured questionnaire during in-person interviews, providing information on infant feeding practices, including breastfeeding, bottle feeding, and mixed feeding, as well as the frequency and duration of these practices. Early childhood caries (ECC) were assessed by two trained examiners using WHO oral health survey methods. In Finland, a cohort study followed preschool children aged 1 to 4 years from 11 daycare centers in Oulu. Data on caries development were collected from dental health records. Breastfeeding lasting one year or more was defined as prolonged breastfeeding. In the UK, the School Heart Health Study surveyed cardiovascular risk factors in children from 10 British towns. Parents completed a questionnaire on infant feeding practices during the first three months of life, including breastfeeding, bottle feeding, and mixed feeding, as well as breastfeeding duration grouped into intervals to minimize recall bias. The Black Women’s Health Study (BWHS) in the United States followed 59,000 Black women aged 21 to 69 years since 1995. Among participants, 4,072 women who gave birth for the first time between 1995 and 2003 were included. Breastfeeding data were collected through questionnaires, and lactation duration was categorized into intervals for analysis. In Kansas, a retrospective cohort study linked data from the Pediatric and Pregnancy Nutrition Surveillance Systems to assess breastfeeding duration and weight status at age 4 years. Breastfeeding duration was categorized into intervals ranging from less than 4 weeks to 52 weeks or more. In Florianópolis, Brazil, a cross-sectional study sampled schoolchildren aged 7 to 14 years from public and private schools using a two-stage probabilistic sampling design. Data on breastfeeding and other control variables were collected through a questionnaire sent to parents or guardians. In Jakarta, Indonesia, adolescents aged 15 to 18 years were recruited from a senior high school. Only those whose mothers could recall breastfeeding duration were included. Breastfeeding duration was categorized into intervals for analysis. In Korea, the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES) collected genetic and lifestyle data associated with chronic diseases in adults aged 40 years and older. At Stanford University Hospital, a cross-sectional study included women aged 40 to 65 years. Participants completed an electronic survey on reproductive and lactation history, with cardiovascular disease as the primary outcome. In Southampton, UK, the Southampton Women’s Survey (SWS) followed non-pregnant women aged 20 to 34 years who later became pregnant. Infants were visited at 6 and 12 months, and milk feeding history was recorded. Breastfeeding duration was defined by the date of the last breastfeed. In the United States, the Women’s Health Initiative (WHI) enrolled postmenopausal women aged 50 to 79 years into clinical trials or observational studies. Participants completed baseline questionnaires on medical, reproductive, and family history, and breastfeeding duration was recorded as a categorical variable. Outcomes included cardiovascular disease and myocardial infarction, confirmed through medical record reviews. In India, a cross-sectional study in Kanpur district recruited preschool children aged 3 to 5 years using a two-stage cluster sampling technique. Mothers completed a pre-tested questionnaire in Hindi, providing information on feeding and oral hygiene practices. In New Zealand, the Auckland Birthweight Collaborative Study followed infants born at 37 weeks or later. Exclusion criteria included multiple births and congenital anomalies. Data on feeding practices and health during the first year of life were collected.
